lesson_title: The Debt That Shrinks From the Wrong End: Annuities
hook_text: Two years of faithful car payments — R133 000 paid. The bank's settlement figure? R167 431 STILL owed. Here's the arithmetic.
clip_script: You borrow 250 000 rand for a car. Five years, one percent a month, instalment 5 561 rand. Two years in, you've paid faithfully — twenty-four instalments, over 133 000 rand. You ask the bank for a settlement figure. They say: 167 431 rand, please. Two THIRDS of the loan still standing. Scam? No — arithmetic. Picture your debt as a water tank. Every month, interest pours in: one percent of whatever is currently in the tank. Your instalment bails out a fixed bucket. Month one, the tank is full — interest pours in 2 500 rand, so your 5 561 bucket removes only 3 061 of real debt. The fuller the tank, the harder interest fights back. Only near the end does each bucket land almost whole. Debt shrinks slowly first, fast last — from the wrong end. But the tank picture hands you the defence: an extra rand paid EARLY strikes the water when it's deepest, cancelling years of the interest that rand would have bred. Early overpayments are worth multiples of late ones. That is annuity mathematics — and it is consumer self-defence.
visual_style: A glass water tank labelled with the loan balance, an interest pipe pouring in at the top and a bucket bailing at fixed size, a split bar in each instalment showing interest versus real repayment shifting over sixty months.
mood: Eye-opening, protective, a friend explaining the fine print.
pacing: Calm setup, a jolt at the settlement figure, methodical through the tank months, empowering close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any loan the way the bank does.
